::: {#rem-incompressible-random}
#### Incompressible strings look random

By @thm-incompressible-strings,
if $x$ is drawn uniformly from the strings of length $n$,
for example by $n$ fair coin flips,
then $\Prf{\ckolmf{x}{n} < n - k} < 2^{n-k} / 2^n = 2^{-k}$.
So a string of $n$ fair coin flips can be compressed by more than $k$ digits
with probability less than $2^{-k}$.
A string with $\ckolmf{x}{n} \ge n$ has no description shorter than itself.
@li2019introduction [chapter 2] call a string random
when it is incompressible in this sense,
for a variant of $\kolm$ whose programs need not be prefix-free.
A proof can pick an incompressible string and show that some property must hold for it,
or else the string would have a short description.
@li2019introduction [chapter 6] call this the *incompressibility method*.

:::
